description: I am a student trying to get the most out of every opportunity he gets and is trying to better himself day by day. Mostly interested in programming but considering my for now lacking skills I will devote myself to bringing out my idea and coming up with suitable solutions for the problems our earth is facing right now.
summary:
I have written a story about the rovers and other equipment that were abandoned up in space. My focus point was bringing out the easiness of understanding and remembering key aspects of the text. Which is why a lot of the complicated technical terms are being omitted. 

This adresses the challenge in the way that it does bring forth the story of most of the technological milestones we have left behind in space but at the same time it gives people who aren't really familiar with space technology or lack the necessary time/knowledge to really comprehend formally written texts about all the space technology drifting through space. 

The importance lies in the fact that anybody from whichever background can read it and get a feel for why it is so important that those machines have existed and because the text is written with a lot of empathy and humanization of the equipment there will be more people capable of resonating with the text rather than needing a degree just to understand the core message. This will bring more people into the topic of space and hopefully give people the necessary drive or kick in order to dive into the vastness of space research. If we manage to bring together people through simpler to understand texts then I believe we can get more researchers and enthusiasts to come together and bring back those treasures of humanity. This in turn will give space technology a massive influx of funds and human resources that hasten the advance of humanity into space
details:
The text brings forth the curiosity of humanity that is required in order to dive into all the complicated facets that space technology has to offer.

Most people can't get themselves involved into difficult to understand topics and like easier to messages that get a clear answer on what is right and wrong. For space and it's endless mass of uncertainties along with unknowns most people get scared or don't see the point in starting something they can't see the end of.

That's exactly why my story can give those very people a small taste for what space can actually be about and how interesting it can actually be. It might not be the most scientifically correct text or the story with the most including facts but because of that it can be a spark that ignites the flame of thirst for knowledge that every human possesses.

The text is typed in the most classic and most used software: word. A lot of students and adults working office jobs have used the microsoft office softwares at least once or read pdf files that were made in word. So the familiarity already sets it apart from formally written texts that are made by professors or researchers that sometimes adhere to really strict formatting rules that might be hard to understand or follow for the general public.

My way of handling this challenge is creative in the way that it sets itself apart from the normal and expected approach where I use the most difficult or scientific words. I have to say that it might be because I am a student and because I myself am not particularly well informed on the specifics of space technology or in general all the scientific terms that exist. However I believe that with my experience of knowing what it feels like to not understand a topic or have somebody explain something in a too complicated manner, I can deliver a story that is not too far off on the real specifics while also being down to earth for enough for anybody to understand. A lot of people most likely choose either a experts point of view or try to mimic an experts way of talking to an high degree, yet I have to admit that I am not an expert and don't have the necessary knowledge to even attempt an story that might seem close to the way a scientist with years of experience would write. So I instead chose the complete opposite way. I ran full sprint towards a text that only mentions the key details like the names of the rovers or other aspects while leaving out the other complicated terms that might be important for learning but diffcult for understanding and reading.

In hopes of achieving a better and easier way to get into space technology I stuck to this overly simplified text that might seem to have a lack of substance at first glance but hopefully leads to an increase in space degree aspirants.
